title: What a Telephone Payment on an Auto Loan Comes To
content:
A payment taken from the borrower during a call on a loan of the Auto Loans line must cover three things added together and rounded half-up to the cent: the charges this charter asks that payment to clear, the interest owed on the loan for the days the clock runs, and the scheduled installment.

The charges the payment must clear are all the charges standing unpaid on the loan. The charge allowance set against them is 0.00. The charge allowance is taken off the charges the payment must clear before they are added to the interest and the installment, and the charges after the allowance are never less than nothing.

The clock runs from the date of the last payment credited to the loan, and a further day is added to that span, so the days the clock runs are the days from that date to today together with one more.

The interest is worked out on the unpaid principal at the rate recorded on the loan: the unpaid principal multiplied by that rate, divided by one hundred and then by the product's day count basis, and multiplied by the days the clock runs. The interest so obtained is rounded half-up to the cent.

Once taken, the payment is applied in the order this charter fixes, so the charges standing on the loan are cleared from it first, the interest accrued through the credit date next, and whatever remains goes to principal.

## Worked on hypothetical readings

| Reading | Value |
|---|---|
| Unpaid principal | 18400.00 USD |
| Rate recorded on the loan | 7.99 percent |
| Product's day count basis | 365 days |
| Date of the last payment credited, counted to today | 30 days |
| Charges standing unpaid | 60.00 USD |
| Scheduled installment | 412.00 USD |

The days the clock runs are 30 together with one more, which is 31. The unpaid principal multiplied by 7.99 gives 147016.00; divided by one hundred that is 1470.16; divided by 365 that is 4.027835 and so on, which multiplied by 31 gives 124.862904 and so on, rounded half-up to the cent as 124.86.

The charges the payment must clear are 60.00, and the allowance of 0.00 leaves 60.00.

The payment to take is 60.00 together with 124.86 together with 412.00, which is 596.86.

## The same loan with nothing standing unpaid

Were the charges standing unpaid nothing at all, the same loan would give 0.00 together with 124.86 together with 412.00, which is 536.86. The interest and the installment do not move with the charges.
